inter_coder_reliability.coding_scheme: paper's own codebook (data/codebook.md), binary substantive-vs-not, 77 cells (11 themes x 7 models)
inter_coder_reliability.interpretation: Codebook is reliable (independent coders agree kappa~0.65-0.83); paper's own R1 coding lands at low-moderate agreement with independent recoding (mean kappa 0.44).

hc_robustness.note: 5 of 6 headline HC zones replicate under 4-coder independent consensus; independent coders find MORE consensus overall (7 HC), so paper's claims are conservative.

dependence_analysis.interpretation: Within-US agreement (0.62) equals cross-bloc (0.62); the highest AND lowest agreeing pairs are both same-bloc (US). Shared provenance does not create a dependence structure that inflates consensus. The permutation test is underpowered (p=0.32, 11 themes, high marginals) and cannot reject that convergence matches independent base rates — reported honestly.

data_integrity_flags.codebook_model_names_stale: data/codebook.md lists 2024-era models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5, Grok-2, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen2.5, Mistral Large 2); paper claims 2026 frontier models (Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, etc.)
data_integrity_flags.figure4_vs_table3_mismatch: Figure 4 renders several cells inconsistently with consensus_matrix_r1.csv/Table 3 (e.g. Concentration shown 4/7 in fig vs 5/7 in data; Infrastructure Grok half-mark; apprenticeship half-mark on GPT vs data=Claude-only).
data_integrity_flags.pilot_outputs_in_outputs_dir: outputs/*_output.md are an earlier pilot run (grok-3, dated 2026-03-14) with different word counts; authoritative corpus is data/raw_outputs/round1 (116,082 words, matches paper's ~114k).
